snippets.text: Arena says Meta's Muse Spark Open (Max) is the top US open model in its Code Arena WebDev ranking, with 1511 points, priced at $1.25 and $4.25 per million input and output tokens.
snippets.why: It is the first open-weight Muse Spark model, and Arena says it scores 156 points above Meta's earlier open model, Muse Glimmer.

snippets.text: Tibo Sottiaux (@thsottiaux) says Codex and Work now give users more effective usage, citing context reuse across subagents, longer caching and better request routing that raise cache hits.
snippets.why: The post, labelled Day 12 of a series, had 1,112 likes within hours, and it also says GPT-6 Pro was improved for all Pro users.

snippets.text: Politico reports Anthropic has written its own bill to regulate frontier AI and is pitching it to members of Congress, according to a post by Andrew Curran that cites the report.
snippets.why: Politico's own article was not reachable for this item, so the bill's contents are unconfirmed here.

snippets.text: SemiAnalysis says ByteDance gave apps 30 days to opt out of its Doubao phone agent and 155 did, including WeChat, Taobao, Alipay, DeepSeek and Kimi.
snippets.why: The same post says Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent, so it frames access for AI agents as a growing fight between apps and assistants.

snippets.text: Nvidia says its first PyTorch-CUDA build for Windows on Arm is out, and claims RTX Spark runs coding agents 4.6x faster than Intel's Panther Lake 12Xe.
snippets.why: The figures come from Nvidia's own developer blog and use its AA-AgentPerf-local test with Qwen3.8-27B, so they await independent checks.

snippets.text: Tongyi-MAI released OpenGCUA, an Apache-2.0 research preview with code and trajectories from eight frontier models, and says its approach lifts mean OSWorld-v2 partial score from 45.3 to 64.9.
snippets.why: The repo ships no model yet, only agents, a macOS harness and data, and the gains are the authors' own evaluation.

snippets.text: International Cyber Digest says Unit 42 found hackers spied on government Linux servers for months using AI-written code, and left the AI's chats behind; a fake sudo prompt saved admin passwords.
snippets.why: The claim comes from a social post summarising the report, which was not located, so details are unverified.

snippets.text: OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux posted a video from the ChatGPT Space team, which he says is the actual team working on it, and the post has passed 1,000 likes.
snippets.why: Space is OpenAI's shared workspace for teams, and the post invites users to say what they want built next.

snippets.text: Tibo Sottiaux says ChatGPT Space gained slides support yesterday, available for now on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans while OpenAI collects feedback.
snippets.why: Slides were previewed at DevDay as a collaborative answer to PowerPoint and Google Slides, and are now reaching paying users.

snippets.text: Anthropic says it has given a team from the nonprofit METR inside access to review its AI models and safety practices, The Decoder reports.
snippets.why: It is an outside audit of a lab's models and processes, and the announcement does not say what METR will publish.

snippets.text: Bloomberg reports Anthropic signed its first data-center lease in Canada, buying capacity at an EverWind project in Nova Scotia worth more than C$10 billion, about $7.1 billion.
snippets.why: It is the first Canadian site for a lab that is buying compute in large blocks, though the capacity and start date are not in the summary.

snippets.text: The Decoder reports a new essay argues about 90 percent of neurons in neural networks serve a clear function, and researchers are still debating whether the thesis holds up.
snippets.why: If true, deception or dangerous behaviour could be spotted in a model's circuits directly, which is why safety researchers are watching the argument.

snippets.text: The Verge reports, citing Nieman Lab, that Meta's new business terms, effective 30 October, appear to let it crawl and scrape sites associated with advertisers, including publishers, to train AI.
snippets.why: The wording is read as covering news sites for free, and Meta has not been quoted in the summary on whether that is the intent.

snippets.text: SemiAnalysis says only about 2.3 GW of roughly 21 GW of US data-center capacity in moratorium areas is likely to be delayed, excluding a Texas pause.
snippets.why: It pushes back on the idea that local moratoriums are stopping the US datacenter buildout, and the full analysis is in its newsletter.

snippets.text: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas says Vercel developers can now use Perplexity Decider on Vercel's AI Gateway.
snippets.why: It extends the decision model Perplexity open-sourced this week to the gateway where many teams already route their model calls.
